svg.title: Structure of the Cedar .NET client application
svg.desc: Four layers from top to bottom. Composition: Program.cs reads configuration from appsettings.json, environment variables and user secrets into CedarSettings, creates a logger, asks ConnectionFactory for a connection and runs one use case; it is the only place that knows about files, the console and exit codes. Connection: ConnectionFactory validates the settings, builds a connection string or passes a token provider, creates one ServiceClient and checks IsReady and LastError; ServiceClient uses MSAL for tokens and retries throttled requests. Use case: StatusSync receives an IOrganizationService and a logger, finds each work order by FieldLink ID, asks the rules what to do, and sends an update with only the status column and the row version. Pure rules: StatusRules, StatusFile and CedarSettings validation have no dependency on Dataverse. On the right, tests: rule tests and use case tests with a fake IOrganizationService run without any environment; only the connection layer needs a real environment. At the bottom, Dataverse applies the roles of the connection's identity and runs Cedar's plug-ins on every update.
svg.text: Only one layer knows how to connect; everything else depends on IOrganizationService
Configuration: appsettings.json → environment variables → user secrets (later source wins) → CedarSettings.

No Dataverse, no I/O: which status may follow which, how a feed line is parsed, which settings are missing.
